notes: No cab block — running into tube amp. General-purpose Strokes preset with three snapshots covering clean, dirty, and solo tones drawn from the overall cross-album tonal signature. Not specific to any one song — designed to cover the mood of the most popular tracks across Is This It, Room on Fire, and The New Abnormal. BPM set to 100 as a neutral default — use tap tempo to lock to the specific song being played. Confirmed cross-album rig constants: Visual Sound Jekyll & Hyde OD (Stupor OD), Pro Co RAT (Ratatouille Dist), MXR Micro Amp (Minotaur), Fender Hot Rod DeVille (US Double Nrm, preamp-only). Since the DeVille is a confirmed cross-album rig constant, it's modeled as a US Double Nrm preamp block per AGENTS.md's rule — see note_on_block_limit for how it's routed given the 8-block serial-path limit. Compression (Red Squeeze / MXR Dyna Comp) confirmed on Hammond's board. The telephone filter EQ — aggressive low and high cuts with boosted mids — is the single most defining characteristic of the Strokes' tone across all albums and must be present in all three snapshots.
note_on_block_limit: Path 1A is already at the 8-block limit (Noise Gate, Red Squeeze, Stupor OD, Ratatouille Dist, Minotaur, Parametric EQ, Adriatic Delay, Ganymede). The US Double Nrm preamp block runs in parallel on Path 1B rather than in series on 1A, merging back into the main path before the EQ block — set up the two paths to split after Minotaur and rejoin before Parametric EQ. It's listed in signal_chain at that same point to reflect where it sits in the audio flow, even though physically it occupies a separate path slot, not an additional 1A block.

signal_chain.notes: Clean snapshot most open — compression and very light OD generate minimal noise. Dirty and solo snapshots tighten as Ratatouille Dist generates more noise between notes.

Confirmed on Hammond's board. Provides the consistent, slightly squashed dynamics that are central to the Strokes' compressed, even-attack rhythm character. ACTIVE in all three snapshots at the same settings — compression is a constant tonal foundation, not a snapshot-variable element. Mix at 70% blends compressed and dry signal to maintain some pick attack transient.

Approximates Jekyll & Hyde overdrive side. ACTIVE in Snapshot 1 (clean) at very low Drive — provides the barely-there breakup that gives the Strokes their 'clean but not quite clean' foundation. BYPASSED in Snapshots 2 and 3 — the Ratatouille Dist handles all saturation in the dirty and solo snapshots, and stacking would over-saturate.

Confirmed cross-album Strokes pedal. BYPASSED in Snapshot 1 (clean). ACTIVE in Snapshots 2 and 3. S2 dirty: Gain at 4.5 — close to YAML-documented 'blues type tone' setting (Gain 3.5-4) which gives the gritty, mid-present crunch of the Strokes' driven rhythm tone. Filter at 4.5 — neutral, letting the RAT's natural character through without over-cutting high frequencies. S3 solo: Gain pushed to 7.0 approaching YAML-documented 'lead type tone' setting — more bite and harmonic emphasis for lead lines.

Nick Valensi confirmed notable user per YAML. Approximates MXR Micro Amp clean boost. BYPASSED in Snapshots 1 and 2. ACTIVE in Snapshot 3 only — lifts the solo above the rhythm bed and adds slight Klon harmonic character on top of the Ratatouille Dist. Low Gain to keep it transparent, high Level for the boost.

No dedicated DeVille model exists on Helix LT — US Double Nrm/Twin Reverb is the closest available 6L6 Fender platform per AGENTS.md substitution table. Confirmed cross-album rig constant. Routed on parallel Path 1B rather than stacked onto the already-full 8-block Path 1A — splits after Minotaur and rejoins before Parametric EQ (see note_on_block_limit). Settings held CONSTANT across all three snapshots, same treatment as the Red Squeeze compressor — this represents a fixed physical amp setting (a rig-level characteristic), with the pedals ahead of it (Stupor OD, Ratatouille, Minotaur) doing the per-snapshot dynamic work rather than the amp itself. Kept neutral/mild (low Drive, moderate Master) so it adds gentle amp-front-end coloration and gain-staging support without fighting the telephone filter EQ that follows.

The telephone filter EQ is the single most defining characteristic of the Strokes' tone across all albums. All three snapshots share this fundamental voicing: aggressive low bass cut, boosted mids, rolled-off highs. The specific mid frequency and gain vary per snapshot — clean uses a lower, warmer mid boost; dirty pushes it harder and lower for telephone character; solo opens the high end slightly for lead clarity and raises the mid frequency for more cut.

Tempo-synced to Master BPM (default 100). All three snapshots use eighth note — the most universally applicable Strokes delay division across tempos. Use tap tempo to lock to the specific song. Clean: modest mix for depth. Dirty: low mix — the rhythm tone should be tight and not washy. Solo: higher mix and feedback for the lead lines to bloom. BBD Size 2048 throughout. Rate 0.1Hz, Depth 0 — modulation disabled.

1_clean.Time: 300ms (1/8 at 100 BPM — adjust via tap tempo)

2_dirty.Time: 300ms (1/8 at 100 BPM — adjust via tap tempo)

3_solo.Time: 300ms (1/8 at 100 BPM — adjust via tap tempo)

signal_chain.notes: Short, intimate reverb throughout — the Strokes' recording aesthetic across all albums favors a contained, close-mic'd quality. None of the three snapshots use a long or spacious reverb. Clean is the most reverberant — the slightly open, warm quality of clean Strokes passages benefits from a little air. Dirty is the driest — tight, punchy rhythm tone. Solo opens up moderately for lead lines to breathe. Tone at 4.5 on clean and dirty — slightly darker than neutral, matching the lo-fi recording aesthetic of the classic albums.

1_clean.description: Clean/lightly driven foundation tone. Red Squeeze compressor active throughout. Stupor OD at Drive 3.5 — barely overdriven, the 'not quite clean' compressed character of the Strokes' quieter passages. Ratatouille and Minotaur bypassed. US Double Nrm preamp active (Path 1B) at its fixed mild setting. Telephone filter EQ with mid +3dB at 600Hz. Eighth note delay at 22% mix. Short warm reverb (1.2 sec, 20% mix, Tone 4.5).

2_dirty.description: Driven rhythm tone. Red Squeeze compressor active. Stupor OD bypassed. Ratatouille Dist active at Gain 4.5, Filter 4.5 — RAT blues-type tone setting giving gritty, mid-present crunch, feeding the US Double Nrm preamp (Path 1B) at its usual fixed setting. Minotaur bypassed. Telephone filter EQ pushed harder — mid +4dB at 700Hz, tighter High Cut at 8000Hz. Eighth note delay very low mix (15%) — tight and not washy. Shortest driest reverb (0.8 sec, 12% mix).

3_solo.description: Lead/solo tone. Red Squeeze compressor active. Stupor OD bypassed. Ratatouille Dist at Gain 7.0, Filter 5.5 — pushed toward RAT lead-type setting for more bite and harmonic emphasis. Minotaur active — Gain 2.5, Tone 5.5, Level 8.0 (MXR Micro Amp boost lifting lead above rhythm bed), all feeding the US Double Nrm preamp (Path 1B) at its usual fixed setting. Telephone filter EQ opens slightly — mid frequency at 800Hz, High Cut at 9500Hz. Eighth note delay at 35% mix with more feedback. More reverb (1.5 sec, 25% mix) for lead lines to breathe.

playing_notes.pickup_notes: Neck or middle for Snapshot 1 (clean). Bridge for Snapshots 2 and 3.
playing_notes.tap_tempo: IMPORTANT — default BPM is 100 but should be tapped to match the specific song. Eighth note delay works well across the Strokes' tempo range (approximately 96-120 BPM for most songs). For faster songs like Hard to Explain (~150 BPM) consider switching the Note Sync to 1/16 for a tighter slapback character.
playing_notes.telephone_filter_eq: The mid boost at 600-800Hz combined with Low Cut 100-110Hz and High Cut 8000-9500Hz is the single most important element of this preset. It defines the compressed, slightly nasal, mid-forward character across all three snapshots. If anything sounds wrong, check this EQ block first.
playing_notes.compression: The Red Squeeze compressor at Sensitivity 6.0, Mix 70% is a constant foundation. It provides the even, slightly squashed attack that characterizes the Strokes' rhythm playing — particularly important for Snapshot 1 where the compression does most of the 'controlled' work.
playing_notes.technique: The Strokes' sound relies heavily on playing technique — consistent pick attack, deliberate strumming on rhythm parts, and aggressive digging-in on leads. The Red Squeeze compressor and telephone filter EQ reward firm, confident playing more than soft or tentative picking.
playing_notes.ratatouille_note: The Ratatouille Dist Filter parameter: lower values = more treble (brighter), higher values = more high-frequency cut (darker). At 4.5 in S2 the Filter is neutral. At 5.5 in S3 it cuts slightly more high frequency, giving the lead a slightly smoother, more focused character.
